first_impression: Looks like an unexpectedly authentic sheepdog sim wrapped in a cozy low-poly aesthetic. I came in expecting a basic *Untitled Goose Game* knockoff, but the herding commands, actual sheepdog trials, and wolf threats give it real mechanical teeth.
best_things: The authentic collie control kit (lie down, creep, flank, bark) actually matches real working sheepdog tactics instead of just being an arcade fetch game.
Level variety is shockingly strong, rotating through trials, lost lambs, ram stare-downs, flooding fords, and full night-watch survival.
The charm loadout and star progression give genuine replay value and mechanical flexibility without bloating the cozy scope.

worst_problems.problem: Wolf rescue timer and bridge chokepoints create cheap-feeling fail states when sprinting across water barriers.
worst_problems.suggestion: Give a brief wolf-stalking telegraph before the grab happens so you can intercept before being forced into a frantic 15-second river detour.

worst_problems.problem: Center-screen alert banners and tutorial bubbles directly obscure active field gameplay and flock sightlines.
worst_problems.suggestion: Move event banners (like wolf attacks and tutorial tips) into a dedicated top/bottom notification strip rather than floating near the dog.

worst_problems.problem: Terrain geometry and open pasture expanses look barren, flat, and repetitive between key landmarks.
worst_problems.suggestion: Add more micro-topography, varying grass patches, gorse bushes, and stone walls to break up the flat polygon plane.

worst_problems.problem: Evening numbering is inconsistently labeled across level cards and map slots.
worst_problems.suggestion: Standardize level sequencing so evening numbers consistently match across season map slots, mission intro cards, and debrief screens.

worst_problems.problem: Sheep models are overly rigid polyhedrons that lack expressive movement when bolting or being stared down.
worst_problems.suggestion: Add slight squash-and-stretch or ear/tail jitters to the sheep and ram models so they feel like living livestock rather than rolling geometry.

boredom_points: Traversing back across empty fields to gather one lone wandering sheep after 90% of the flock is already penned.
Waiting out the slow pacing of the long drives in later autumn levels if you've already mastered the flank angles.
confusions: How wolf aggro ranges interact with terrain elevation and river banks.
Whether Wolf Moon mode is a global unlocked difficulty or an opt-in toggle per individual level.
wish_list: An endless pastoral sandbox mode where you just manage an open pasture at your own pace without timers.
Customizable collie coats (tri-color, blue merle, red border collie).
Controller support with dedicated shepherd whistle audio cues mapped to bumpers.
one_line_review: Equal parts cozy country evening and frantic tactical trial - a genuine, mechanically smart border collie sim that punches way above its price tag.
